terms.gloss: the guardian of a child, a woman, or anyone not in charge of his own affairs
evidence: Plaut. Truc. 859: quī suīs tūtōrem mēd optāvit līberīs
Cic. Att. 12.28.3: tūtor sum līberīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From tueor. It does not mean a teacher.

phrases.latin: Videō eccum quī suīs tūtōrem mēd optāvit līberīs.
phrases.english: Ah, there I see the man who chose me as guardian for his children.

sources: Lewis & Short: tutor
